title: Question 4
stem:
A metal block hangs vertically from one end of a spring. The other end of the spring is tied to a
thread that passes over a pulley and is attached to a vibrator, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

parts.label: (a)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
T = 0.60 s and ω = 2π / T; ω = 10 (10.47) rad s-1
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The vibrator is now switched on.
The frequency of vibration is varied from $0.7f$ to $1.3f$ where $f$ is the frequency of vibration of the block in (a).
For the block, complete Fig. 4.3 to show the variation with frequency of the amplitude of vibration. Label this line A.

markscheme_points.text: sketch: smooth curve in correct directions
amplitude never zero and line extends from 0.7f to 1.3f

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some light feathers are now attached to the block in (b) to increase air resistance.
The frequency of vibration is once again varied from $0.7f$ to $1.3f$. The new amplitude of vibration is measured for each frequency.
On Fig. 4.3, draw a line to show the variation with frequency of the amplitude of vibration.
Label this line B.
